GIVEAWAY OR TRUISM CANDIDATES

rewrite.reason: Outdated product name. The verifier labelled it weak_card, but the fact and answer are sound and the only defect is the retired name 'Route 53 Resolver'. resolver.html: 'Route 53 VPC Resolver was previously called Route 53 Resolver, but was renamed when Route 53 Global Resolver was introduced.' rewrite.statement: Route 53 VPC Resolver query logs can include repeated queries that VPC Resolver answers from its cache.
rewrite.explanation: VPC Resolver query logging records only unique queries. A repeat that VPC Resolver answers from its cache within the TTL leaves no new log entry.
rewrite.misconception: VPC Resolver query logs record every DNS query an instance sends, including repeats answered from cache.

rewrite.reason: explanation_error: the explanation did not say where the key ARN goes, and it left out the key-policy requirement. The statement and answer are unchanged. Page: 'If you choose SSE-KMS, you must use a customer managed key ARN. If you use a key ID, you can run into a LogDestination undeliverable error... you must update the key policy... so that the log delivery account can write to your S3 bucket.'
rewrite.statement: VPC Flow Logs requires a customer managed key ARN for an Amazon S3 destination that uses SSE-KMS.
rewrite.explanation: With SSE-KMS on the flow-log bucket, name a customer managed key by its ARN; a key ID can cause a LogDestination undeliverable error. The key policy must also let the log delivery account write.
rewrite.sourceTitle: Required key policy for use with SSE-KMS

rewrite.reason: ambiguous: hibernation writes RAM to the root volume, so the unqualified 'can capture RAM' was defensible as True. The statement now names a running instance and drops the hedge. The source moves from the whitepaper PDF to the EBS page: 'The snapshot includes only the data that was written to the volume at the time the snapshot was requested. It does not include data that has been cached by applications or the operating system.'
rewrite.statement: An EBS snapshot of a running EC2 instance's volumes preserves the instance's RAM contents for forensic analysis.
rewrite.explanation: An EBS snapshot holds only data written to the volume when the snapshot was requested, excluding data cached by applications or the OS. Memory evidence needs a separate capture.
rewrite.misconception: Snapshotting a running instance's volumes also captures what is held in its memory.

rewrite.reason: source_problem: the old source was a Cognito blog post, and the 'For CloudFront requests' qualifier was outdated because JA3 inspection is 'available only for Amazon CloudFront distributions and Application Load Balancers'. The new source is the WAF request-components page: 'This fingerprint serves as a unique identifier for the client's TLS configuration... to match with any future requests that have the same TLS configuration.' I dropped the resource qualifier and shortened the statement to keep 3.1's true and false lengths within 5 characters. The fact and answer are the same.
rewrite.statement: An AWS WAF JA3 match can follow a client across changes in its source IP address.
rewrite.explanation: JA3 is a hash of the TLS Client Hello that identifies a client's TLS configuration. An exact string match on it catches later requests with that configuration, whatever their source IP.

If your IAM credentials expire, the connection continues to persist... you can set a SSH timeout value to terminate the SSH session automatically.' New factKey: instance-connect-session-outlives-credentials, difficulty 2.
rewrite.statement: An EC2 Instance Connect SSH session stays open after the IAM credentials behind its key push expire.
rewrite.explanation: IAM authorizes only the public-key push. The SSH connection lasts until the session ends, so cutting access means closing the session or setting an SSH timeout on your own client.
rewrite.sourceTitle: Connect to a Linux instance using EC2 Instance Connect

rewrite.statement: Route 53 VPC Resolver returns SERVFAIL by default when DNS Firewall fails to respond.

cards.statement: Route 53 VPC Resolver query logs can include repeated queries that VPC Resolver answers from its cache.
cards.explanation: VPC Resolver query logging records only unique queries. A repeat that VPC Resolver answers from its cache within the TTL leaves no new log entry.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. resolver-query-logs.html: 'VPC Resolver query logging logs only unique queries, not queries that VPC Resolver is able to respond to from the cache... The second query is not logged.' The rename to the current product name is correct.

cards.reason: Both lenses keep. Every clause is on flow-logs-s3-cmk-policy.html: customer managed key ARN, the key-ID LogDestination undeliverable error and the key-policy update for the log delivery account.

cards.statement: An AWS WAF JA3 match can follow a client across changes in its source IP address.

cards.reason: Both lenses keep. waf-rule-statement-fields-list.html calls JA3 a unique identifier for the client's TLS configuration that matches future requests with the same configuration (CloudFront and ALB). 'can' covers the shared-fingerprint caveat.

Confirmed on ec2-instance-connect-methods.html: 'An IAM policy attached to your user authorizes this action' (push); 'The duration of the connection is not determined by the duration of your IAM credentials... you can set a SSH timeout value'.
